description: Log the stress signals around a borrower since a date: lender actions, debt quotes, lawsuits, liens, layoff notices and adviser hires, each graded by severity. Credit alpha.
suggested_questions: Log early warning signals for Optimum Communications (optimum.com), ticker OPTU, since 2026-05-01.
Log early warning signals for Brightspeed (brightspeed.com), a private company owned by Apollo, since 2026-05-01.
Log early warning signals for New Fortress Energy (NFE, newfortressenergy.com) since 2026-05-01.
skill:
Where distress shows up before a default:
- Debt and liquidity: amendments, waivers and forbearance in 8-Ks and lender filings; revolver draws; amend-and-extend;
  a switch to paid-in-kind interest; distressed exchanges, uptier and drop-down transactions, assets moved to
  unrestricted subsidiaries; missed or deferred payments; going-concern language; late filings (NT 10-K, NT 10-Q);
  rating actions published openly.
- Lender actions: cooperation agreements and ad hoc groups reported in press, non-accrual footnotes and sharp
  markdowns in BDC schedules of investments, lenders hiring advisers.
- Market prices: loan and bond quotes printed in public articles, with the earlier quote the same page gives.
- Legal and liens: suits by vendors, landlords, lenders and customers for non-payment, judgments, tax and mechanics
  liens on open state or county portals, regulator fines, bankruptcy filings by affiliates. CourtListener, state court
  portals and claims agent sites (Kroll, Epiq, Stretto, Omni).
- Operations: state WARN layoff databases in the states with the company's largest sites (state, site, date,
  headcount), closures, lost contracts, recalls, stoppages, licence losses, cyber incidents.
- People and advisers: CEO, CFO, treasurer, general counsel or auditor departures; a chief restructuring officer;
  restructuring directors joining the board; restructuring advisers or counsel hired, and whose side they are on.
- Counterparties: stretched supplier payments, tightened vendor terms, withdrawn trade credit insurance, a key customer
  or supplier in distress, landlord action.
- Names: the parent, borrower and issuer entities and trade names often differ; every source is searched by each.

Severity:
- high: a default or an event that usually precedes one by weeks: missed payment, forbearance, going-concern
  language, restructuring advisers or a CRO hired, lenders organised under a cooperation agreement, loan on
  non-accrual, distressed exchange, rating at CCC or selective default, debt quoted below 70, a reported plan to file.
- medium: pressure that usually precedes a default by months: covenant amendment or waiver, revolver fully drawn,
  switch to PIK, downgrade or negative outlook, debt quoted between 70 and 90, CFO or auditor departure with no named
  successor, WARN notices covering a site closure, several vendor or landlord suits, late filing, amend-and-extend at a
  higher spread.
- low: worth logging and common at healthy companies. Growth financing, routine refinancing at similar terms and
  ordinary executive hires are not stress.
- An event at a lender, sponsor or fund is not an event at the borrower unless it concerns this borrower's debt.

Where the alpha is: WARN notices, vendor suits and lender footnotes appear weeks before a downgrade or a default
headline.

Citations and evidence:
- source_url is one full public https URL: the exact page the value was read on. Never a search results page, an index
  page, an internal file path or a source id. A value from two pages is two values.
- Dates are the date the event happened or the source printed, as YYYY-MM-DD, not today's date.
- Public pages only. Paywalled, logged-in or leaked material, expert-network transcripts and anything marked
  confidential carry MNPI risk and are out of bounds. When only a paywalled article's headline and first lines are
  public, those lines can be used, marked "Headline only:".
- Evidence grades: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or
  archived page being measured), company_statement, original_press, repeated_press, third_party_tracker. When a page
  repeats a filing, a release or another outlet, the original is the better citation.
- A value nobody published is null. Not an estimate from memory. Analyst opinions, estimates, price targets and
  ratings are views, not evidence.
- Entity drift is the most common error: a namesake, a parent, a subsidiary, a lender or a sister company. Match on
  legal name, ticker, SEC CIK or domain before using a page.

output_schema.description: Stress signals for one borrower since a date.

signals.description: One row per stress event on or after the since date, newest first.

items.description: One row per stress event on or after the since date, newest first.

key.description: Stable lowercase identifier for this item, built from fixed parts joined by underscores (e.g. us_doj_hsr, first_lien_term_loan_2031, q3_2026_earnings). The same item gets the same key in every run.

what_happened.description: Event, with names, case numbers and figures as printed.

party.description: Lender group, court, counterparty, person or firm involved.

figure.description: Amount, headcount or price, plain number.

severity.description: Severity under the definitions in the agent's knowledge.

evidence.description: Evidence grade of the source: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or archived page being measured), company_statement (the company describing itself), original_press (an outlet's own reporting), repeated_press (a page repeating another outlet), third_party_tracker (a site compiling data from elsewhere).

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.
